title: Lifting tail density through dense singleton fibres
statement:
Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $T$ be a compact Hausdorff space, $V$ a Hausdorff space, and $q:T\to V$ a continuous surjection. Suppose $S\subseteq T$ is dense and $q^{-1}(\{q(s)\})=\{s\}$ for every $s\in S$. Let $v:\mathbb N\to V$ satisfy: for every nonempty open $B\subseteq V$ and every $N\in\mathbb N$, there is $k\ge N$ with $v_k\in B$. For every nonempty open $U\subseteq T$, the set
$$B_U=V\setminus q(T\setminus U)=\{y\in V:q^{-1}(\{y\})\subseteq U\}$$
is nonempty and open. Consequently, for every $N\in\mathbb N$ there is $k\ge N$ such that the nonempty fibre $q^{-1}(\{v_k\})$ is contained in $U$.

proof.text: Fix a nonempty open $U\subseteq T$. For $y\in V$, membership $y\notin q(T\setminus U)$ says that there is no $x\notin U$ with $q(x)=y$. This is equivalent to every $x\in q^{-1}(\{y\})$ lying in $U$. Hence $B_U=V\setminus q(T\setminus U)=\{y\in V:q^{-1}(\{y\})\subseteq U\}$. This is a pointwise set identity and does not require surjectivity.

proof.text: The complement $C=T\setminus U$ is closed in the compact space $T$. By [lem-weil-pbc-closed-in-quasi-compact], $C$ is quasi-compact in its induced topology. Restrict $q$ to $C$; this map $q|_C:C\to V$ is continuous, since the inverse image of an open $W\subseteq V$ is $C\cap q^{-1}(W)$, open in $C$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-image-quasi-compact] to this restriction: its image $q(C)$ is quasi-compact in $V$. As $V$ is Hausdorff, [lem-sfb-compact-subset-hausdorff-closed] makes $q(C)$ closed in $V$. Therefore its complement $B_U$ is open.

proof.text: Choose $u\in U$. Density of $S$ means $u\in\overline S$, so its open neighbourhood $U$ meets $S$; take $s\in S\cap U$. By hypothesis $q^{-1}(\{q(s)\})=\{s\}\subseteq U$, and the set identity of Step 1 gives $q(s)\in B_U$. Thus $B_U$ is nonempty. Equivalently, if $q(s)=q(x)$ for some $x\notin U$, the singleton-fibre hypothesis forces $x=s\in U$, a contradiction.

proof.text: Let $N\in\mathbb N$. Steps 2 and 3 show that $B_U$ is nonempty and open, so the assumed tail condition for $v$ gives $k\ge N$ with $v_k\in B_U$. Step 1 yields $q^{-1}(\{v_k\})\subseteq U$. Surjectivity of $q$ gives an $x\in T$ with $q(x)=v_k$, proving that this fibre is nonempty. Since $U$ and $N$ were arbitrary, this proves every asserted clause.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q156-649bdb4ad (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: The statement is unchanged and there are no new nodes; this is not a re-split, since the item was statement-only, created by Q117. Step 1 is a pointwise identity B_U = {y : fibre ⊆ U}. Step 2 follows the proof of Stacks 08YD (topology.tex lemma-closed-map, line 3257) through three Mathlib-leaf nodes whose statements I checked: lem-weil-pbc-closed-in-quasi-compact (005C) gives that C = T∖U is quasi-compact; lem-weil-pbc-continuous-image-quasi-compact (04Z9(1)) is applied to the continuous restriction q|_C; lem-sfb-compact-subset-hausdorff-closed (08YB(1)) makes q(C) closed in Hausdorff V. Step 3 uses density to find s in S∩U, whose singleton fibre puts q(s) in B_U, and does not need U saturated. Step 4 applies the tail property to the nonempty open B_U and gets a nonempty fibre from surjectivity. Every hypothesis is used except Hausdorffness of T, which is harmless. Edge cases U=T, T empty, finite discrete T and multi-point fibres outside q(S) all hold. The parent lem-sfb-countable-split-profinite-cover uses exactly this conclusion with S = Γ.
